diagnostic_first_index_baseline.description: Sanity check on a Discussion claim that the engine's own option ordering is strong and naive re-scoring can lose to just picking index 0
diagnostic_first_index_baseline.conclusion: Our heuristic overrides are net-positive, not fighting the engine's ordering

note: vs-random win rate (84.7%) is lower than exp010's simple deck (97%), but the direct head-to-head (72%) is a much larger, more reliable signal per the project's own established lesson (vs-random is a weak predictor of real strength). Loss reasons vs random are dominated by real combat outcomes (68%), not structural collapse -- the deck is fundamentally sound; the vs-random gap likely reflects the agent not fully exploiting the richer trainer package (Tool/Stadium/multi-Supporter decisions still fall back to generic flat scoring).
